key.description: The agent's key (a17): what every other field and call names it by.

name.description: Its name within its workspace (designer). A rename changes it and nothing else.

workspace.description: The key of its workspace (w2); workspaces.list gives the workspace's name.

lead.description: Whether it is its workspace's lead: what is sent to the workspace reaches it.

owner.description: The key of the person who owns it (p1); people.list gives the person's name.

role.description: The first line of the agent's ROLE.md that is not blank and not a heading, as one line, at most 160 characters; empty when there is none.

state.description: The session's lifecycle word for the state column only: one of x-state-words, lower case; an open set, clients treat an unknown word as idle. It is not whether the agent is working: an agent idle at its prompt with background work running is state idle and status.state running. Whether an agent is working is status.state, and nothing else.

background.description: What runs behind the agent's prompt now, oldest first: its background shells and monitors, and its subagents, a foreground one while the turn waits on it. Empty when nothing runs. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

servers.description: The TCP ports the agent's processes (those load.get attributes to it) listen on, lowest port first; empty when none. The session's own are left out: its claude or codex process and that process's direct children that are not a shell (MCP and LSP servers), so a server started through its Bash tool stays; so are the daemon's and the panes'. Read every 15 s; a change is an agent.changed. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

account.description: The account the agent is on: the one its session runs on, or, at rest, the one whose prompt cache still holds its conversation, until cache_until. null at rest once cache_until has passed or is null: the agent is on no account and counts on none. Its next wake goes to the account with the most weekly headroom (furthest behind its pace line, Account.pace; with pacing off, the most left of its weekly window), carrying the conversation there; it starts fresh from its handoff only when the conversation cannot be carried. While the cache lives a wake stays on its account, unless that account cannot run it now (its wall, its pace, no free slot), when the usual moves apply.

task.description: The task the agent holds in doing; null when it holds none, or only a queued, blocked or ended one.

ctx_pct.description: Whole percent of the context window the agent's own session has used; null when it has no account, no session of its own, or a usage snapshot too old to trust. A view without the field is the same as null.

input_holders.description: Who holds the input; one in v1, a list so more can later. A structured agent has no input to hold: [].

state_detail.description: The text drawn beside the state word (a clock, what a wait is for), at most 40 characters; empty when there is none. The state column is drawn from state and state_detail alone.

text.description: From the running turn's newest tool call: its `tool`, a space and the first line of the call's description (Bash says what the command does there), else of its chat.transcript tool item's `text`, or the tool alone when both are empty; cut to 60 characters (Unicode code points, no ellipsis).

doing.description: What a running agent is doing now, for the line under its name: while state is running and handoff is null, a client draws it in place of status.text. null when no turn runs or the turn has called no tool yet. Absent from a daemon that does not send it. A change of doing alone is pushed (agent.changed) at most once every 5 s, with the newest value.

started.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): whether the agent has ever run (a state row exists).

has_repo.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): whether its config names a repo.

has_terminal.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): whether a terminal is recorded for it.

screen_word.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): the word the screens draw for its state (RUNNING, IDLE, PENDING, MOVING, DIALOG, FATAL), `tui.screen_state`'s and not the wire `state`; null when it never started.

screen_detail.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): the text drawn beside screen_word.

unreached.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): requests, messages and answers owed to it that have not reached it.

words.description: The daemon's reason the task waits.

task_waits.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): its tasks that wait on a hold, oldest first.

wake_wait_reason.description: Only with agents.list `status: true` (what `hl team` draws): what holds back a wake that is due (set only while would_wake is true).

structured.description: The agent is set up to run as a structured session, whether its session is live or closed: chat.send returns a receipt for it, and it has no terminal to watch. Absent means false (a terminal agent). Sent in agent.changed too.

kind.description: What the agent is, for a column (agents.kind): the model and its effort as `<model> <effort>`, effort one of low, mid, high, xhi, max (any other effort is shown whole), with the vendor in front as `<vendor> <model> <effort>` only when it is not claude. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

task_role.description: The role of the tasks it owns (Task.role): check when its row says role: check, else work. Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

task_count.description: The tasks the agent owns that are not done: the current one and those waiting (queued or doing). A draft that is not the current task is not counted, as it is not approved yet; one the agent picked up and made current is. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

ready.description: The agent is idle (the screen word IDLE), has a current task, that task is queued, and no open blocker holds it: it can be given work now. Absent means false.

account.description: The account whose window the wake waits on.

clock.description: When that window rolls over, as unix seconds: the shortest walled window, the longest when only that stands. Null when the reset is not known or the wait is for a slot (the account is at its cap), not a window.

assumed.description: The account is a guess (nothing has confirmed the one the resume is tied to), not the account itself.

wall.description: What holds back a wake that is due (the screens' wall cell): the account that would wake it. Null when would_wake is false or nothing holds it back. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

fire.description: A trigger about to fire (the home row's warning cell): the daemon would hand this agent off at its next tick. `usage` is the shortest window at the wall, `usage_7d` the longest, `context` the context at its limit. Null when none, and for an agent whose triggers do not apply (closed, no terminal, parked, throttled or degraded). Needs a live evaluate over the agent's current usage and context readings, not a stored value. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

cache_ignored.description: The agent's resume reuses its session whatever the prompt cache did (its own ignore_cache_expiry, else the global one), so a countdown from cache_until means nothing. Read from configuration. Absent means false.

config_error.description: Why the agent's configuration cannot be read, as one line; null when it can. When set, `kind` is absent (and the model, effort and the other fields that come from the configuration are null or absent). Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

needs_you.description: Set while the agent waits on a decision only a person at its terminal can make. Fed by hooks (PermissionRequest and the permission and question Notification kinds) and by the session file saying status `waiting` with `waitingFor` (`permission prompt` is the one measured; the file has no needs or tempo key), never by reading the screen; the tool and its target come from the PermissionRequest hook event; cleared by the hook that follows (PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd) or when the session file stops saying it. While set, except for kind `switch_offer`, `state` is `waiting`, `has_dialog` is true and `attention` is `alert`. null when none.

cause.description: Why the conversation is ending: the words of session.cause (`context_full`, `move`, `settings_applied` for changed settings, `restart` for a person's Restart, and the trigger's own word for the rest, such as `usage` or `login`). An open set.

phase.description: `waiting`: a restart for changed settings waits for the turn under way to end. `writing`: the agent writes its handoff note and the daemon takes the record. `starting`: the old session is closed and the new one is launching.

settings.description: The settings a restart for changed settings applies, in launch order (`model`, `effort`, ...). Absent for any other cause.

handoff.description: Set while a session hands off or restarts, so a chat that sits still can say why. Cleared when the new session's start item appears. Every change is an agent.changed. A handoff that waits for a usage window to reset shows `writing` only; it is not `starting` until a launch is due. null when none. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it.

cause.description: Why it is switching, in the words of handoff.cause: `usage`, `usage_7d`, `usage_early`, `move` for a person's order, `login`, `ended`, `pinned`. An open set.

phase.description: `saving`: the limit was reached and its progress is being saved; `to` is not decided. `switching`: the old session is closing for `to`. `starting`: the session on `to` is launching. `waiting`: it stays on `from` until `until`, because the account resets soon or no account has room.

from.description: The account it is leaving, or waits on.

to.description: The account it goes to, null while saving or waiting.

until.description: When a wait ends, null for any other phase.

account_switch.description: The account switch the agent is in, from the limit being reached until the new session has started, written as each step begins; every step is an agent.changed. null when none. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it.

text.description: The whole body of its newest request to the founder (a say, ask or decision), whether or not it was read.

last_to_founder.description: The agent's newest request to the founder; null when it never wrote to them. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

founder_unread.description: How many of the agent's open requests to the founder they have not seen yet (past the for_you_seen cursor, as `hl inbox` counts them; founder_seen is that cursor), less the asks its task comments raised, which have cards of their own. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet.

founder_seen.description: The highest message number of this agent the founder has had in view (the for_you_seen cursor chat.seen moves); 0 when none. A chat opens at the first of the agent's messages above it, under an unread divider. Absent from a daemon that does not serve it yet: no divider.

status.description: What it is doing and why (x-status). Absent from a daemon that does not send it.

AgentView.description: The stored per-agent view; the daemon decided every field.

repo.description: owner/repo of the worktree's origin when it is on GitHub (https or ssh), else null.

oneOf.description: Terminal handle for terminal.attach. Null for a structured agent.

session_open.description: A session is running. For a structured agent, its session is live (terminal is null).

account_pick.description: The account the daemon would place a session start on, before session.start; account null with a reason when none can take work.

prompt.description: The agent's open prompt, or null.

cwd.description: The directory a shell command for this agent runs in: its worktree when that is on disk, else the daemon's home directory. worktree.path is what the agent's record holds and may name a directory that is gone; cwd is always usable.

can.description: Whether each action of the chat page's menu is worth offering now, by the daemon's own rules: ok, and why not when it is not.

kind.description: The recorded event kind; open set. state, task_delivered, handoff, key, input, interrupt, start and stop are expected once those are recorded.

text.description: One line to show; falls back to the kind.

operation.description: The id of the operation; operation.get and the operations topic follow it.

OperationStarted.description: The result of a write that starts a long-running operation.

AgentSettingValues.description: An agent's settings, every value a string as `hl agent set <agent> key=value` takes it. Keys an agent may change on itself: model, effort, context_k, handoff_note. Every other key is the founder's (an agent proposes it with proposal.propose kind settings).

browser.description: custom is read-only: set in a terminal.

context_k.description: Handoff threshold in thousands of tokens, a whole number.

idle_close.description: Idle close in whole minutes, 0 never, empty follows the global park_timeout_s.

sandbox.description: Why a key, not an is_off/back_on pair: it is already an agent setting (agents.sandbox_on, `hl agent set sandbox=on`), read in AgentDetail.settings and written the same way as every other key. `on` takes effect at once (the key and the grant go now; a running session restarts on the next idle sweep). `off` needs the founder's grant.

kind.description: permission: a tool or a folder waits for a yes. question: the agent asked the person something. usage: the session limit's choice, only while the daemon is not handling that limit itself (x-dialogs usage_limit_choice). dialog: any other (a start-up dialog the daemon will not answer included), and any the daemon does not know: unknown is a person. stuck: the daemon retried, restarted and relaunched the agent and it is still stuck: one card, gone when the trouble is. trust: the vendor waits at its folder-trust screen. start_failed: the last starts failed and the agent is stalled. no_session: wakes were made and no session started. switch_offer: the agent is parked at its usage limit because no account has room to spare, and it may start on `account` now (agent.switch_now). Not answering keeps it waiting, so unlike every other kind it does not set `state` to `waiting` or `has_dialog`, and it tells no stall. The same event is never two cards, and a load hold is never stuck.

title.description: The card's title: plain, one line, at most 40 characters, chosen from the kind and where it came from. daemon: 'Waiting for folder trust' (trust), 'Stuck at a start-up dialog' (a start-up dialog it will not answer), 'Stuck at a dialog' (a dialog it cannot get past), 'Stuck after restarts' (stuck), 'Won't start' (start_failed), 'Woke but didn't start' (no_session), 'No account has room to spare' (switch_offer). hook, session: 'Waiting for your OK' (permission), 'Asked you a question' (question), 'Usage limit: choose what to do' (usage), 'Waiting at a dialog' (dialog).

text.description: The card's description, a full sentence under the title, from the hook, the session file or the daemon's record; never read from the screen. It does not name the agent: the card is in that agent's chat.

source.description: hook: the PermissionRequest hook. notification: Claude Code's Notification hook, a prompt nobody answered. session: the session's own file (sessions/<pid>.json status waiting and waitingFor). daemon: the daemon's own record (a start-up dialog it will not answer, a dialog it cannot get past, an agent it could not heal); never a task.

account.description: The account a switch_offer offers, the one closest to having room, asked again at each change of the view. Absent for any other kind.

Grant.description: A path the founder let an agent read (x-access).

path.description: Absolute, as granted; a folder covers everything under it.

AccessChanged.description: access.changed: an agent's grants after a change (x-access).

BackgroundJob.description: One piece of work running behind an agent's prompt.

kind.description: shell: a command run in the background; monitor: a Monitor tool watch; subagent: an Agent tool call.

label.description: What it is, in at most 100 characters: the call's description, else a shell's command, else, for a subagent, its subagent_type.

foreground.description: Subagents only: true while the agent's turn waits on it, false when it runs in the background.

AgentServer.description: One TCP port a process of an agent listens on.

address.description: The address it listens on: 127.0.0.1 or ::1 (this machine only), 0.0.0.0 or :: (every interface), else the interface's. A process on several addresses of one port is one entry, the first of 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::1, ::.

command.description: The command line of the process that listens, as ps shows it, cut to 120 characters.

methods.name: agents.list
methods.summary: The rail: the stored view of every agent.

schema.description: Add the status-line fields of each agent (started, has_repo, has_terminal, screen_word, screen_detail, unreached, task_waits, wake_wait_reason), read at the call; screen_word and screen_detail may be as old as the stored view. Default false.

methods.name: agent.get
methods.summary: One agent: the view plus session and terminal facts.

methods.name: subagents.counts
methods.summary: How many subagents run now and how many started today, per agent and per account.
methods.description: A start counts as running until a SubagentStop of the same session, or until that session ends (its SessionEnd, a new session of the agent, or the agent's session closed). today counts starts since local midnight. An account is the one the start was recorded on. An agent or account with neither is absent.

methods.name: pr.exists
methods.summary: Which of the numbers are pull requests (open, merged or closed) in the repo of the agent's worktree.
methods.description: numbers holds at most 20 integers, else -32602 bad_request naming `numbers`. The daemon asks GitHub with its own gh login, so a private repo answers. repo is null, and found empty, when the agent has no worktree or its origin is not on GitHub. A number that is a PR is remembered for good, one that is not for about a minute. When gh fails, found is empty and nothing is remembered.

methods.name: agent.timeline
methods.summary: The agent's recorded events, newest first.

schema.description: Return rows older than this id.
Default 50, at most 200.

methods.description: Today this is the agent's generic recorded events (the daemon's events table, rows of that agent): id is the event's id and `before` an event id; kind is the recorded kind; actor is the payload's `actor` when it is an object, else null; text is the payload's `text`, else `detail`, else `method`, else the kind; data is the whole payload ({} when it has none). State changes, deliveries and key presses appear only once they are recorded as events, which a later task does; clients must not expect them, and must treat kind as an open set.

methods.name: agent.options
methods.summary: What the new-agent form offers.

methods.name: agent.set
methods.summary: Change an agent's settings: an agent its own ordinary keys, the founder any.

params.name: restart
params.description: How the restart that applies a changed setting to a live session goes: resume (the same conversation, the default) or fresh (a handoff note, then a new conversation).

methods.name: agent.fold
methods.summary: Run hl fold for an agent.

methods.name: agent.move
methods.summary: Move an agent to another account.

methods.name: agent.switch_now
methods.summary: Start an agent waiting at its usage limit on the account a person chose, or the one with the most room, now: the answer to a needs_you of kind switch_offer. Only the room test is skipped: an account at a limit, one with no free slot and a pin still refuse.

params.name: account
params.description: The account to start on; absent, the one with the most room.

methods.name: agent.unstall
methods.summary: Clear a STALLED agent: it goes to queued with its failure counters reset, as hl unstall does. Refused (gate state) when the agent is not stalled.

methods.name: agent.force_start
methods.summary: Let work that the machine's load or an account's pace holds for an agent (status reason load or pace) go past them once, and agent.timeline records it (load_limit_passed, or pace_passed). The call answers once the start has begun at the next tick (a launch or a wake), or is refused with why it failed; other calls on the connection are answered meanwhile. Past 10 minutes what let it past is taken back, nothing is started and the call is refused (gate state). Refused (gate state) when neither holds anything of the agent's.

methods.name: agent.retire
methods.summary: Retire an agent, as an approved retire does: its row and its scheduling row are deleted, its folder (ROLE.md, memory, settings) moves to agents/archive/<date>-<name>, and its build caches are removed. Its past messages, requests and events stay. Its git worktrees go first, and an agent whose worktree cannot go is not retired, so no worktree is left with nobody's name on it: one that is merged into main, clean and no other agent's is removed with its branch (`git branch -d`); one that holds work (commits not on main, files not committed) goes as `worktree` says. Without `worktree`, such a worktree refuses the call (gate `dirty`, with `worktrees` [{path, files_changed, commits_ahead}] in the error data) and nothing is retired: the app asks the founder and calls again with the answer. `keep` keeps the worktree, and so the agent: refused, gate `worktree`. A locked worktree always refuses it the same way, and one on no branch or on main does unless `worktree` is `force`. When git then fails to remove one, nothing is retired either (gate `state`, with git's reason); a worktree removed before the one that failed stays removed. The plain-words reason names the worktree and why. One another agent also works in, the repository's own checkout and one that is gone already are left as they are. An HR retire that is applied carries no answer, so a worktree that holds work refuses it, as it does a running agent's retire that finds one at its turn's end: the apply fails (apply_failed) with the reason, the agent and its worktrees stay, and no task is opened. Work is saved only when the founder answers save. The tick judges a worktree an agent left when it launched in another (after a rename or a move), unless an agent still records it: merged and clean it is removed with its branch; holding work it stays and the founder gets a decision task tagged `worktree-removal`. Its body says in plain words what would be lost and carries `Path:` and `Member:` lines. Its answers are the words keep, save and force, which the app shows as the buttons Keep the worktree, Save to a branch, then delete and Force delete; force needs no second confirm. The answer is carried out before the task closes, the task's verdict says what was done, and an answer that cannot be carried out leaves the task open. `said` says which. Founder only. The call answers only once the retire has run, with its outcome: `said` for what was done, or the refusal. For an agent with a session running it waits for the turn running now to end (a session at its prompt is closed at once; a turn is never cut), up to 10 minutes; still running then, it is refused (gate state) and nothing is deleted. Other calls on the connection are answered meanwhile. Refused (gate state) while another agent reports to it or hangs under its name (<agent>.<rest>): the reason names them. An agent the daemon does not have is not_found.

schema.description: The founder's answer for a worktree of the agent that holds work: save (what is left is committed to a new branch rescue/<agent>-<date>, then it is removed) or force (removed with whatever it holds; its branch stays; it also removes one that is on no branch or on main, never a locked one). keep keeps the worktree, so the agent is not retired (gate worktree). Another word is bad_request, field worktree.

methods.description: Its turns on open tasks come off: the top one is sent back to the agent below it with the note `retired` (not counted as bounced), and one lower down just goes.

methods.name: agent.create
methods.summary: Register a new agent, give it a worktree on a branch of a repo, and start it there, as hl spawn does. The call answers only once the operation ended: done, with the operation id and the start's words in said, or refused (gate state) with the reason, the operation id and whether the agent was registered. The operations topic sends operation.progress along the way, and other calls on the connection are answered meanwhile. A create still running after 10 minutes cannot be undone half way: the call is refused naming the step it reached and the operation id, and the operation goes on to done or failed. Founder only. Parameters are checked before anything is looked up, in this order: request_id, name, role, effort, account, then the repo, the parent, the name against its parent, and whether the name is used.
methods.description: The operation has kind agent.create and its agent is the new name from the first event. steps_total may be null while it is unknown; a client shows step as the daemon sent it and invents none. When it is done, result is {agent, registered: true}. When it failed, result is {agent, registered}: registered says whether the agent was added to the team before the failure, so a failed operation can leave a registered agent that is not started; nothing is cleaned up. A name already used by an agent is refused (gate state) and no operation starts. A name with a parent must be '<parent>.<rest>'; anything else is bad_request, field name. base omitted means the daemon's default branch name, which is main today; a client that knows the repo's default_branch sends it.

schema.description: A free string today.
A directory, as repos.list gives it in path. An unknown one is not_found, what repo.
The branch to start from. The worktree takes the side, local or origin/, that leads, and the operation fails when they have diverged.
Not served: bad_request, field account, never dropped. A new agent's account is chosen when it starts; a client offers no account picker until a daemon serves this.

methods.name: session.start
methods.summary: Launch a session for the agent, optionally on a named account: in its terminal, or for a structured agent as a structured session with no terminal.

schema.description: The Go daemon does not place sessions on a named account yet: it answers bad_request, field account, never drops it. A client offers no account picker until then.

methods.name: session.wake
methods.summary: Resume a closed session.

methods.name: session.stop
methods.summary: exit asks Claude to quit; close ends the session and keeps the terminal; kill ends the process.
methods.description: An agent may call it for mode exit and close; mode kill is refused to the agent role (`refused`, gate `role`) before the agent is looked up, because it ends another session mid-turn with no handoff record. Kill is for a person. For a structured agent exit and close are the same: the daemon ends the CLI's input and waits for it to exit, and kill ends its process group. Close mid-turn is refused (gate state): interrupt first.

schema.description: close only: the next start is a fresh session.

methods.name: session.restart
methods.summary: Restart a session.

methods.name: session.compact
methods.summary: Hand the session off and start a fresh one, as a full context does.
methods.description: The handoff a full context runs (the agent's note, the record, a fresh session), once the turn under way has ended; the call answers at once and AgentView.handoff shows the rest. A closed agent restarts fresh from its record, as session.restart with fresh does; one mid-handoff is refused (gate state).

methods.name: session.park
methods.summary: Park an agent.

methods.name: session.input
methods.summary: Type text at the prompt; Enter optional.

schema.description: Default true.

methods.description: Refused at a shell prompt (gate state, reason 'nothing sent - a shell prompt is showing'): the daemon types nothing when the pane shows a shell, since a line there would run as a command. session.type and session.keys are not checked this way. Refused with gate screen_blocker while the screen shows a dialog or one the daemon does not recognise, which includes the moments right after a wake, before the screen has been read: nothing is typed; session.keys and terminal.input are the way through (they pass an open dialog), or call again once the screen reads. Each call is recorded as an event of the agent (kind type, key or input) whose actor is the caller: for a paired device, kind device with its id. A daemon that runs structured agents need not serve this method (the Go daemon does not: it is absent from hello, so a client never calls it for one). One that serves it refuses an agent run as a structured session, gate unsupported: it has no terminal to type at, so a client sends chat.send and watches the transcript.

methods.name: session.keys
methods.summary: Named keys for menus and dialogs.

schema.description: esc, enter, up, down, tab, shift-tab, ctrl-c, 0-9.

methods.description: Each call is recorded as an event of the agent (kind type, key or input) whose actor is the caller: for a paired device, kind device with its id. A daemon that runs structured agents need not serve this method (the Go daemon does not: it is absent from hello, so a client never calls it for one). One that serves it refuses an agent run as a structured session, gate unsupported: it has no terminal to type at, so a client sends chat.send and watches the transcript.

methods.name: session.type
methods.summary: Plain typing into the pane: characters sent as typed, no Enter, no prompt checks.

schema.description: Printable characters and tab; no other control characters (those are session.keys).

methods.description: Which call sends text when: session.type is what a person typing in the pane uses, with input.take first; it passes the wall and any open dialog, as the keys would. session.keys sends named keys (menus, dialogs, ctrl-c). session.input sends a whole prompt line for the daemon's own flow and is refused (gates wall, screen_blocker) while a usage wall or a dialog is up, since a typed line would answer the dialog. Each call is recorded as an event of the agent (kind type, key or input) whose actor is the caller: for a paired device, kind device with its id. A daemon that runs structured agents need not serve this method (the Go daemon does not: it is absent from hello, so a client never calls it for one). One that serves it refuses an agent run as a structured session, gate unsupported: it has no terminal to type at, so a client sends chat.send and watches the transcript.

methods.name: session.interrupt
methods.summary: Stop the turn in progress (Esc for a terminal agent; a control request to the CLI for a structured one).
methods.description: For a structured agent no terminal lock or input hold applies, and it is refused (gate state) when no turn is running, so a stale button learns why.

methods.name: session.launch_prepare
methods.summary: Build and record the launch `hl launch` becomes; the caller locks its worktree and execs the answer.

schema.description: The absolute folder the launch runs in; the session's working directory.
The caller's own arguments for the vendor (what follows -- in hl launch), e.g. --resume <id>.
Override the usage wall.
A file holding the session's opening prompt; taken (read, then removed) once the launch is built.
A destination someone already chose; else the daemon picks the account with room.
What the session's start is recorded as; launch when empty.
Who asked for it.
The caller's environment, which the session's starts from.
The vendor's binary found on the caller's PATH; the daemon looks it up itself when empty.
The hl the vendor's hooks call.
The terminal pane the caller runs in; empty with none.
The folder that pane runs in.

env.description: The session's whole environment, as KEY=VALUE.

warnings.description: What the person at the terminal should read before it starts.

methods.description: For the process that runs hl launch, before it is any agent's session: no agent identity is needed, but only the local socket serves it (gate role elsewhere), the agent must be one the daemon knows (not_found otherwise), and the pid recorded for the session's proof is the peer's own, never the request's. A launch that must not go ahead (no room, an account not logged in, at its usage limit, a pane opened for another agent, nothing to resume) is refused with gate state and the reason in words for the person at the terminal. On success the daemon has recorded how the session starts (its start row, the terminal, the account, the launch fingerprint) and taken the handoff, so the caller must exec.

methods.name: prompt.list
methods.summary: The open permission prompts and dialogs.

methods.name: prompt.answer
methods.summary: Answer the prompt the caller saw; if it changed nothing is sent.

oneOf.description: Keys of the picked options, for a prompt with `multi`; may be empty.

schema.description: A PromptOption.key, or {text} for the free-text answer to a dialog that asks for one; a text answer passes the same gates and the prompt check. An array only answers a `multi` prompt.
With choice deny on a prompt whose source is hook: a short reason, given to the agent with the deny. bad_request (field note) on any other answer.

methods.description: For a structured agent's permission prompt the choice is one of its option keys, allow or deny; yes, no or esc is bad_request (field choice). No terminal lock or input hold applies. A prompt whose source is hook is answered the same way, allow or deny, through the call that is waiting on it (permission.ask).

methods.name: permission.ask
methods.summary: An agent's session asks the founder whether it may run a tool call, and waits for the answer.

schema.description: The tool's name, as the PermissionRequest hook gives it.
The tool call's input as the hook gives it (tool_input): for Bash, command and description.

behavior.description: The founder's answer; null when the call ended with none (an hour passed), and the agent's own dialog shows in its terminal.

message.description: With deny: what the agent is told, with the founder's note when one was given.

methods.description: Called by `hl hook PermissionRequest`. Raises a Prompt of kind permission, source hook, with options allow and deny, and holds the call until prompt.answer answers it, the caller hangs up, or an hour passes. One such prompt per agent is open at a time; a second call waits for the first to close. Nothing is typed into the agent's terminal. Refused for a caller that is not an agent's session.

methods.name: input.take
methods.summary: Become the one who types at this terminal.

schema.description: Take the input from the person or device that holds it instead of being refused; the holder notice tells them. It never types into the agent's own turn: typing still waits for it.

methods.description: A daemon that runs structured agents need not serve this method (the Go daemon does not: it is absent from hello, so a client never calls it for one). One that serves it refuses an agent run as a structured session, gate unsupported: it has no terminal to type at, so a client sends chat.send and watches the transcript.

methods.name: input.release
methods.summary: Hand the terminal back to the daemon.
methods.description: A daemon that runs structured agents need not serve this method (the Go daemon does not: it is absent from hello, so a client never calls it for one). One that serves it refuses an agent run as a structured session, gate unsupported: it has no terminal to type at, so a client sends chat.send and watches the transcript.

methods.name: agent.strip
methods.summary: The line under an agent's chat header: model, account, context, prompt-cache life and the screen word.

ctx_pct.description: Percent of the context window used, as far as the session's own report is trusted.

ctx_limit.description: The window the model has, with the agent's own setting applied.

cache_left_s.description: Seconds until the prompt cache lapses; negative once it has; null with nothing to measure from.

screen_word.description: The agent's state as the screens draw it (`tui.screen_state`), not the wire `state`; null when it never started.

methods.description: Context figures come from the usage snapshot of the agent's own session, so they are null for an agent with no account or no snapshot.

methods.name: progress.get
methods.summary: The caller's progress note: the one on its request in progress, else on the task it holds, else on the agent (what hl progress shows with no note).

note.description: The note, or null when none is kept.

methods.name: say
methods.summary: A message typed at once; needs no answer, starts no work, and carries no task: what is written on a task is a comment (task.comment.add).

schema.description: Markdown. It may name images (x-attachments, texts).

Absolute paths of images the message carries (ChatMessage.attachments): PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most 10 MiB each, at most 6. The daemon reads each and keeps a copy under its home. An agent may name only files under its worktree, its folder or the scratch folder; the founder any. A path outside those, a file that is not an image, or an image whose first bytes do not match its ending is bad_request (field files); the message is not written.

methods.name: agent.triggers
methods.summary: What the daemon would decide for an agent right now (hl triggers).
methods.description: One row per agent the daemon knows, in name order; with `agent`, that agent's row alone, and an agent the home does not have is not_found. `fired` is whether the next tick would hand it off; `reason` is the trigger's reason, or for an agent whose triggers do not apply, what holds it (a walled wake, its state until its wake, or no session).

methods.name: access.grant
methods.summary: The founder lets an agent read a path outside its worktree, once or always.

schema.description: An absolute path to a file or folder.

applies_from.description: now: the running session was given the path; next_session: from the next one.

methods.description: See x-access. An agent or member caller is refused, gate role. A path not absolute is bad_request, field path; one that does not exist is not_found, what path; an unknown agent is not_found, what agent.

methods.name: access.revoke
methods.summary: The founder takes back an agent's grant of a path.

removed.description: false when the agent had no grant of that path.

methods.description: See x-access. A path never granted is accepted with removed false, so a retried tap is no error. A path not absolute is bad_request, field path; an unknown agent is not_found, what agent. An agent or member caller is refused, gate role.

methods.name: access.list
methods.summary: The paths the founder granted an agent, newest first.
methods.description: See x-access. Only grants: the roots every session reads are not listed. An unknown agent is not_found, what agent; an agent or member caller is refused, gate role.
